subject: Mathematical Literacy

topics.name: FINANCE
subtopics: Financial documents: tax documents (tax rate tables, IRP5, employee income tax), loan documents (statements, changing loan agreements)
Taxation: personal income tax, taxable and non-taxable income, rebates, UIF (maximum amount), VAT (15%)
Tariff systems (compare 2 or more): electricity, telephone, municipal, bank, transport - via tables, graphs and formulae
Income, expenditure, profit and loss (large organisations, fundraising): two-year comparisons; projected vs actual budgets
Cost price and selling price; percentage profit; break-even values from formulae and graphs

topics.name: DATA HANDLING
subtopics: Developing questions on national and global issues; developing and using collection instruments (interviews, questionnaires, recording sheets)
Classifying and organising: numerical and categorical data, class intervals, tallies, frequency tables
Summarising: quartiles, inter-quartile range, percentiles; measures of central tendency and spread
Representing, interpreting, analysing: pie charts, histograms, bar graphs, line and broken-line graphs, scatter plots, box-and-whisker plots

topics.name: PROBABILITY
subtopics: Probability of simple events (dice, coin games, national lotteries, gambling, insurance risk assessment)
Relative frequency and theoretical probability
Compound events: tree diagrams and two-way tables

topics.name: FINANCE
subtopics: Interest and banking: hire purchase, residual/balloon payments, loans; interest rate, interest, repayments
Banking: investments and insurance plans (interest, interest rate, charges, monthly payments)
Inflation: buying power and prices over time; interpret and analyse graphs
Exchange rates: currency relationships and buying power

topics.name: MEASUREMENT
subtopics: Conversions: factors and tables; metric to imperial and back; °C to °F and back
Time: transport timetables (bus, train, taxi), production schedules (e.g. building a house), tides
Perimeter and area; length, distance and time; cost calculations may apply
Volume and surface area; rates (speed, costing); mass/weight
BMI: formula (kg/m²) and interpreting charts

topics.name: MAPS, PLANS & OTHER REPRESENTATIONS OF THE PHYSICAL WORLD
subtopics: Scale (ratio and bar): actual lengths and distances from scale; determining a scale for drawings and models
Maps: grid references, compass directions, slope on maps

sba: Mid-year examinations (two papers, 100 marks, 2 hours each)

topics.name: MAPS, PLANS & OTHER REPRESENTATIONS OF THE PHYSICAL WORLD
subtopics: Plans: assembly diagrams and instruction manuals; plan symbols, notation and terminology; actual dimensions from a given scale; choosing a suitable scale; drawing 2D floor and elevation plans
Models: packaging problems, 3D scale models, 2D pictures; item arrangement and material-quantity estimates

sba: Preparatory examination (two papers, 150 marks, 3 hours each)

topics.name: REVISION
subtopics: Finance; data handling; measurements; maps and plans; probability

sba: No SBA task for term 4 (final NSC examination)

paper1.format: Q1: 20% at level 1; Q2: Finance; Q3: Data handling; Q4-5: integration of finance, data handling and probability

paper2.format: Q1: 20% at level 1; Q2: Maps and plans; Q3: Measurements; Q4-5: integration of maps & plans, measurements and probability

notes: CAPS p.15: concepts must not be taught in the absence of contexts - learners must meet them in realistic scenarios
Requisite pre-knowledge across all terms: Grade 11 content
Term 1 lists FINANCE twice deliberately: documents/taxation/tariffs early in the term, interest/banking/inflation/exchange rates at the end
